cards.name: ICUIDataContext
cards.summary: Data context of CorelDRAW's UI data-binding framework (the XML-defined dockers and dialogs): a named registry of data-source objects that UI controls bind to, plus a call that opens a dialog bound to it.
use_for: custom docker or add-on UI whose controls bind to script data
checking which categories a context supports (HasCategory) before binding add-on UI to it
avoid: drawing or document automation: it is UI plumbing only, use the Document / Shape API
unattended pipelines that would call ShowDialog: it opens a dialog and presumably waits for it (unverified)
cards.how: Reach the top-level context with Application.FrameWork.Application.DataContext (ICUIApplication.DataContext); CreateChildDataContext makes a temporary child. Add-ons put their objects in with AddDataSource and fetch them with GetDataSource; ShowDialog opens a dialog by GUID against this context.

key_members.name: CreateChildDataContext
key_members.use: temporary child context, optionally limited to a comma-separated category list

key_members.name: Categories
key_members.use: comma-separated list of the categories this context implements

key_members.name: HasCategory
key_members.use: True when the context supports one category

key_members.name: AddDataSource
key_members.use: add a named data-source object; returns its ICUIDataSourceProxy

key_members.name: GetDataSource
key_members.use: proxy of a data source by name

key_members.name: ShowDialog
key_members.use: show a dialog by GUID bound to this context; returns a Boolean (modal, unverified)

gotchas: ShowDialog presumably blocks the COM call until a person closes the dialog (unverified; it returns a Boolean)
dialog GUIDs and built-in data-source names are not in the type library; they come from the workspace XML (unverified)
a child from CreateChildDataContext is temporary; what you add to it presumably disappears with it (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim ctx As Object, p As Object
Set ctx = Application.FrameWork.Application.DataContext
Debug.Print ctx.Categories
If ctx.HasCategory("MyAddon") Then Set p = ctx.GetDataSource("MyAddonDS")

review.changes: ShowDialog modality was stated as fact, now marked unverified; use_for said HasCategory checks data-source registration, reworded to categories

cards.name: ICUIDataSourceFactory
cards.summary: Factory interface the UI framework calls to create an add-on's data-source object when a bound control first needs it; a script gets one by wrapping its own factory object with ICUIApplication.CreateDataSourceFactory.
use_for: registering an add-on data source that is created lazily when its docker opens
avoid: one-off scripts: add the object directly with DataContext.AddDataSource instead
cards.how: Set f = Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateDataSourceFactory(myFactoryObject), then Application.FrameWork.Application.RegisterDataSource "MyDS", f. The framework calls f.CreateDataSource(name, proxy); your object returns the data source and keeps the proxy for UpdateListeners.

key_members.name: CreateDataSource
key_members.use: called by the framework with the source name and its ICUIDataSourceProxy; returns the data-source object

gotchas: you do not call CreateDataSource yourself; the framework does
call ICUIApplication.UnregisterDataSource when the add-on unloads, or the framework may keep a dead object (unverified)
whether a VBA class module works as the wrapped factory object is unverified; .NET add-ons are the usual host (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim cui As Object, f As Object
Set cui = Application.FrameWork.Application
Set f = cui.CreateDataSourceFactory(New MyDSFactory) ' exposes CreateDataSource
cui.RegisterDataSource "MyDS", f, "MyAddon", False

cards.name: ICUIDataSourceProxy
cards.summary: Handle the UI framework gives a data source so it can talk back: tell bound controls which properties changed, and get, set or invoke data-source members by name.
use_for: refreshing a custom docker after the script changes its values
reading or setting an add-on data source's properties from another macro
avoid: changing document content: it only moves values between script objects and UI controls
cards.how: Returned by DataContext.AddDataSource / GetDataSource and passed as Proxy to a factory's CreateDataSource. Keep it in the data source and call UpdateListeners with the names of the properties you just changed.

key_members.name: UpdateListeners
key_members.use: notify bound controls; one comma-separated string of property names

key_members.name: GetProperty
key_members.use: read a data-source property by name

key_members.name: SetProperty
key_members.use: write a data-source property by name

key_members.name: InvokeMethod
key_members.use: run a data-source event handler by name

gotchas: controls do not refresh on their own: skip UpdateListeners and the docker shows stale values
UpdateListeners takes one comma-separated string, not an array
InvokeMethod passes no arguments (only MethodName is harvested)
cards.example:
Dim p As Object
Set p = Application.FrameWork.Application.DataContext.GetDataSource("MyDS")
p.SetProperty "Caption", "Ready"
Debug.Print p.GetProperty("Caption")
p.UpdateListeners "Caption"

cards.name: ICUIDockHost
cards.summary: One node of a frame window's docking layout: a horizontal or vertical split holding dock items (document tab groups or nested dock hosts), into which views can be inserted or split.
use_for: arranging two document views side by side for comparison
reading the workspace layout before taking screenshots
avoid: changing a layout in a CorelDRAW session someone else is using
docker panels: show or hide them with FrameWork.ShowDocker / HideDocker
cards.how: Start at Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.RootDockHost (or FrameWindow.DockHosts) and walk Children / ParentDockHost. InsertView and InsertViewHost move a view or a tab group into this host at Index; the cuiDockOperation argument picks a plain insert or a split.

key_members.name: ParentDockHost
key_members.use: the host this one sits in

key_members.name: DockItem
key_members.use: this host seen as an item of its parent

key_members.name: InsertView
key_members.use: dock a view window here; returns the new view host

key_members.name: InsertViewHost
key_members.use: dock a whole tab group here

gotchas: Orientation is read-only: change the layout by inserting with a split operation
InsertView returns the view host it created; InsertViewHost returns nothing
this rearranges the user's workspace; restore it or work only in a session you own
cards.example:
Dim root As Object
Set root = Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.RootDockHost
root.InsertView ActiveWindow.ViewWindow, 1, cuiDockOperationSplitBottomRight
Debug.Print root.Orientation, root.Children.Count

cards.name: ICUIDockHosts
cards.summary: Collection of all dock hosts (layout split nodes) owned by one frame window.
use_for: listing a window's layout nodes
finding a dock host by its ID
avoid: looking for documents: walk FrameWindow.ViewHosts or the Documents collection instead
cards.how: Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.DockHosts (ICUIFrameWindow.DockHosts). Index with Item, look up by ID with Find, or loop with For Each.
gotchas: Item index base is not stated in the type library; CorelDRAW collections are normally 1-based (unverified here)
Find takes the host's ID string, not a caption
cards.example:
Dim h As Object
For Each h In Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.DockHosts
  Debug.Print h.ID, h.Orientation, h.Children.Count
Next h

cards.name: ICUIDockItem
cards.summary: One child slot inside a dock host: either a document tab group (view host) or a nested dock host, with its index, relative size and screen position.
use_for: resizing the split between two document panes
walking the layout tree generically
avoid: sizing docker panels or the application window: use the frame window's Position instead
cards.how: From DockHost.Children.Item(i), ViewHost.DockItem or DockHost.DockItem. Check Type (cuiDockItemDockHost / cuiDockItemViewHost) and then read ViewHost or DockHost. RelativeSize is writable.

key_members.name: ViewHost
key_members.use: the tab group, when Type is a view host

key_members.name: DockHost
key_members.use: the nested split, when Type is a dock host

key_members.name: Index
key_members.use: position within the parent dock host

key_members.name: RelativeSize
key_members.use: share of the parent's space relative to siblings (writable)

gotchas: only one of ViewHost / DockHost applies; check Type first (the other is presumably Nothing, unverified)
RelativeSize is a proportion against siblings, not pixels
cards.example:
Dim it As Object
For Each it In Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.RootDockHost.Children
  If it.Type = cuiDockItemViewHost Then it.RelativeSize = 50
Next it

cards.name: ICUIDockItems
cards.summary: Collection of the immediate children of one dock host (each a view host or a nested dock host).
use_for: walking one level of the docking layout
avoid: a flat list of every view: use FrameWindow.ViewHosts
cards.how: ICUIDockHost.Children, e.g. Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.RootDockHost.Children.
gotchas: Item index base is not stated in the type library; CorelDRAW collections are normally 1-based (unverified here)
only immediate children; recurse through DockHost.Children for nested splits
cards.example:
Dim kids As Object
Set kids = Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.RootDockHost.Children
Debug.Print kids.Count, kids.First.Type, kids.Last.Index

cards.name: ICUIFrameWindow
cards.summary: A top-level CorelDRAW window (the main frame or a floating frame made by CreateFrameWindowForView): caption, min/max/restore state, Windows handle, tiling, and the view and dock hosts it owns.
use_for: restoring a minimized CorelDRAW before screenshots or UI automation
getting the HWND to target PostMessage / UI Automation instead of global keystrokes
tiling open documents for a side-by-side check
avoid: closing documents: close the Document, not the frame
any Close call in a CorelDRAW session that holds documents you did not open
cards.how: Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow, or Application.FrameWork.FrameWindows.Item(i).

key_members.name: Activate
key_members.use: bring this frame to the front

key_members.name: IsActive
key_members.use: True when this frame is active

key_members.name: IsMainFrame
key_members.use: True for the main application frame

key_members.name: TileViews
key_members.use: tile contained views; True = horizontally (default), False = vertically

key_members.name: CombineViews
key_members.use: put all views back into one tab group

key_members.name: DockHosts
key_members.use: layout split nodes in this frame

key_members.name: Close
key_members.use: close the window and every view in it

gotchas: Close closes the window and all its views; on the main frame that can take down documents you do not own
a minimized frame makes screenshots come back blank; check State and Restore first
Handle is typed long; HWND values fit in 32 bits on Windows, so it is usable on the 64-bit app
Position may be a read-only rectangle; whether editing it moves the window is unverified
cards.example:
Dim w As Object
Set w = Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow
Debug.Print w.Caption, w.Handle, w.State
If w.State = cuiWindowStateMinimized Then w.Restore
w.TileViews False

cards.name: ICUIFrameWindows
cards.summary: Collection of CorelDRAW's top-level frame windows (the main frame plus any floating document frames).
use_for: finding floating frames created by tearing off a document tab
listing every window handle
avoid: listing documents: use Application.Documents
cards.how: Application.FrameWork.FrameWindows (ICUIFrameWork.FrameWindows).
gotchas: Item index base is not stated in the type library; CorelDRAW collections are normally 1-based (unverified here)
the main frame is in the list too; test IsMainFrame before closing anything
cards.example:
Dim w As Object
For Each w In Application.FrameWork.FrameWindows
  Debug.Print w.ID, w.Caption, w.IsMainFrame
Next w

cards.name: ICUIFrameWork
cards.summary: Root of CorelDRAW's UI framework: command bars, main menu, status bar, dockers, dialogs, message boxes, warnings, frame windows, the task manager and the Automation object that runs commands by GUID.
use_for: running a menu command by GUID (Automation.InvokeItem) when the DOM has no call for it
showing or hiding a docker from a macro
getting the main window's handle via MainFrameWindow
avoid: unattended runs that would reach ShowMessageBox (it waits for a button) or ShowDialog (may wait, unverified)
document edits that the Document / Shape API already covers
cards.how: Application.FrameWork (IVGApplication.FrameWork). The interface is flagged hidden in VGCoreAuto.tlb, so the VBA Object Browser hides it unless hidden members are shown; late-bound calls still reach it.

key_members.name: Automation
key_members.use: ICUIAutomation (hidden, described as internal): InvokeItem runs a command by GUID

key_members.name: IsDockerVisible
key_members.use: True when the docker is shown

key_members.name: AddDocker
key_members.use: add a custom docker from a .NET assembly

key_members.name: ShowDialog
key_members.use: show a dialog by GUID (returns nothing; HideDialog closes it)

key_members.name: ShowMessageBox
key_members.use: message box; returns the clicked button (modal)

key_members.name: TaskManager
key_members.use: run tasks on the UI thread or in background

key_members.name: CreateFrameWindowForView
key_members.use: float a view in a new frame window

gotchas: flagged hidden: absent from the Object Browser by default but reachable as Application.FrameWork

ICUIAutomation is itself flagged hidden and its type-library description reads 'Internal Automation - Do not use'; InvokeItem works in practice (the CDR menu harvest is invoked through it) but has no documented contract
ShowMessageBox blocks the COM call until a person answers; whether ShowDialog blocks is unverified (it has a HideDialog pair)
docker, dialog and command GUIDs are not in the type library; take them from the workspace XML (unverified)
ImportWorkspace changes the user's workspace (unverified whether it switches the active one at once)
Name's description says get/set but the harvest marks it read-only
cards.example:
Dim fw As Object
Set fw = Application.FrameWork
Debug.Print fw.MainFrameWindow.Caption, fw.FrameWindows.Count
fw.Automation.InvokeItem "a604992c-e7a6-4a72-85c1-4fcf0ec8ff77"   ' Edit > Select All > Objects (GUID from the CDR menu harvest)

review.changes: added gotcha that Automation is hidden and described 'Internal Automation - Do not use'; FrameWork.ShowDialog (void, has HideDialog) was called modal, now unverified; example used placeholder GUIDs, now a real InvokeItem GUID from the CDR menu harvest

cards.name: ICUIImageList
cards.summary: Keyed list of icons or images that the UI data-binding framework feeds to controls, for example the icons in a custom docker's list box.
use_for: icons for a custom docker or add-on UI
avoid: putting an image into the drawing: use Layer.ImportEx or Layer.CreateBitmap
cards.how: Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateImageList (ICUIApplication.CreateImageList), or the creatable ImageList coclass. AddImage takes a key and a file name, byte array or stream.

key_members.name: AddImage
key_members.use: add an image from a file path, byte array or stream, optionally capped at MaxSize; returns success

key_members.name: AddBitmap
key_members.use: add an ICUIBitmapImage under a key

key_members.name: ImageExists
key_members.use: True when a key is present

gotchas: AddImage and RemoveImage report failure through their Boolean result; check it (whether they also raise is unverified)
ImageCount's description says 'returns all the images' but it is a Long count
MaxSize 0 presumably means no size cap (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim il As Object
Set il = Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateImageList
If Not il.AddImage("logo", "C:\icons\logo.png", 32) Then Debug.Print "load failed"
Debug.Print il.ImageCount, il.ImageExists("logo")

cards.name: ICUIScreenRect
cards.summary: A screen rectangle in pixels with edges, size and centre, plus geometry helpers (move, resize, offset, inflate, union, intersect, hit test); returned as the Position of windows, views and dock items.
use_for: reading where CorelDRAW's window or a document view sits on screen before a capture
computing click points or crop boxes for UI automation from window geometry
avoid: document geometry: shapes use document units through Shape.GetBoundingBox, not screen pixels
cards.how: Read Position on ICUIFrameWindow, ICUIViewWindow, ICUIViewHost, ICUIDockHost or ICUIDockItem, or make one with Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateScreenRect(Left, Top, Width, Height).

key_members.name: SetPosition
key_members.use: set left, top, width and height in one call

key_members.name: Inflate
key_members.use: grow each side by an amount

key_members.name: CopyAssign
key_members.use: copy position and size from another rectangle

gotchas: rectangles from window Position can be read-only: edit a GetCopy
values are screen pixels; on a scaled (high-DPI) display they may not match physical pixels (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim r As Object
Set r = Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.Position.GetCopy
r.Inflate -10, -10, -10, -10
Debug.Print r.Left, r.Top, r.Width, r.Height, r.IsPointInside(r.CenterX, r.CenterY)

cards.name: ICUIStatusText
cards.summary: Small UI object holding a caption string and an optional bitmap, made by ICUIApplication.CreateStatusText. It presumably feeds status or label text with an icon to bound UI controls; which control consumes it is not confirmed.
use_for: status text with an icon inside a custom add-on UI (unverified consumer)
avoid: progress or messages in an automated run: log from the script instead
text in the drawing: use Layer.CreateArtisticText
cards.how: Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateStatusText, then SetCaptionText and SetBitmap.
gotchas: creating one does not by itself show anything on screen (unverified); it has to be handed to a bound control
cards.example:
Dim st As Object
Set st = Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateStatusText
st.SetCaptionText "Exporting 3 of 12"

cards.name: ICUIWarning
cards.summary: One of CorelDRAW's 'don't show this again' warning dialogs: its ID, title, text, an Enabled switch, and a call that shows it only when enabled.
use_for: switching off a specific warning that would otherwise stop a batch macro
showing your own add-on warning that users can suppress
avoid: general message boxes: use FrameWork.ShowMessageBox
leaving warnings disabled after the run: restore Enabled
cards.how: Application.FrameWork.GetWarning(warningID) (ICUIFrameWork.GetWarning).

key_members.name: DoWarningDialog
key_members.use: show the warning if enabled; returns the clicked button

gotchas: warning IDs are not listed in the type library
Enabled = False presumably persists like ticking 'don't show again' (unverified); set it back when done
DoWarningDialog is modal when the warning is enabled; flags are Windows MB_ values and the result a Windows button id
the meaning of GetWarning's bHidden argument is not documented in the harvest
cards.example:
Dim w As Object
Set w = Application.FrameWork.GetWarning("<warning id>")
Debug.Print w.Title, w.Enabled
w.Enabled = False   ' restore to True after the batch

cards.name: ICUIRunningBackgroundTask
cards.summary: Handle to a task started with TaskManager.RunInBackground: abort it, wait for it, change its priority, or finalize it once it is done.
use_for: long add-on jobs (scans, file checks) that should not freeze the UI
avoid: plain VBA macros: CorelDRAW's object model is normally driven from the UI thread
WaitUntilDone on the UI thread for a task that needs the UI thread
cards.how: Returned by Application.FrameWork.TaskManager.RunInBackground(priority, task). Inherits TryAbort from ICUIRunningTask.

key_members.name: TryAbort
key_members.use: stop it from starting or ask it to quit early; does not block

key_members.name: FinalizeIfDone
key_members.use: finalize if complete; returns True when finalized; does not block

gotchas: cuiTaskPriority values are out of order: kMaybeLater 0, kLater 1, kASAP 3, kSoon 4
WaitUntilDone blocks the calling thread; on the UI thread with a task that calls RunOnUIThread it would deadlock (unverified)
the task object must implement ICUIBackgroundTask; doing that from a VBA class is unverified
cards.example:
Dim t As Object
Set t = Application.FrameWork.TaskManager.RunInBackground(kSoon, New MyBgTask)
If Not t.FinalizeIfDone Then t.Reprioritize kASAP

cards.name: ICUIRunningTask
cards.summary: Base handle for a running UI-framework task; its one call asks the task not to start, or to quit early.
use_for: cancelling a queued or running add-on task
avoid: waiting for or finalizing background work: use ICUIRunningBackgroundTask, which adds those calls
cards.how: You get the derived ICUIRunningBackgroundTask from Application.FrameWork.TaskManager.RunInBackground; this is its base.

key_members.name: TryAbort
key_members.use: prevent start or request an early quit; returns at once

gotchas: TryAbort does not wait: the task may still be running when it returns
cards.example:
Dim t As Object
Set t = Application.FrameWork.TaskManager.RunInBackground(kMaybeLater, New MyBgTask)
t.TryAbort   ' returns at once; the task may still be finishing

cards.name: ICUITask
cards.summary: Interface you implement for a unit of work that TaskManager.RunOnUIThread executes on CorelDRAW's main UI thread; its single method is called by the framework.
use_for: add-on code on a worker thread that must touch the document safely on the UI thread
avoid: ordinary macros, which already run on the UI thread
cards.how: Implement it in your own class, then pass an instance to Application.FrameWork.TaskManager.RunOnUIThread.

key_members.name: RunTask
key_members.use: called by the framework to do the work; never call it yourself

gotchas: do not call RunTask yourself; the task manager does
RunOnUIThread blocks until RunTask finishes
implementing it from a VBA class module (Implements ICUITask) is unverified; .NET add-ons can implement it
cards.example:
' class module MyUITask
Implements ICUITask
Private Sub ICUITask_RunTask()
  Debug.Print "on the UI thread"
End Sub
' caller: Application.FrameWork.TaskManager.RunOnUIThread New MyUITask

cards.name: ICUITaskManager
cards.summary: CorelDRAW's task scheduler: runs a task on the main UI thread (blocking) or queues one in the background with a priority and returns a handle to it.
use_for: add-ons that do heavy work off the UI thread and post results back
avoid: simple macros: call the object model directly
cards.how: Application.FrameWork.TaskManager (ICUIFrameWork.TaskManager).

key_members.name: RunOnUIThread
key_members.use: run an ICUITask on the UI thread; blocks until complete

key_members.name: RunInBackground
key_members.use: queue an ICUIBackgroundTask at a cuiTaskPriority; returns ICUIRunningBackgroundTask

gotchas: the task objects must implement ICUITask / ICUIBackgroundTask; from VBA that is unverified
cuiTaskPriority values are out of order: kMaybeLater 0, kLater 1, kASAP 3, kSoon 4
touching the document object model from a background task is presumably unsafe; hand it back via RunOnUIThread (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim tm As Object, bg As Object
Set tm = Application.FrameWork.TaskManager
tm.RunOnUIThread New MyUITask                     ' Implements ICUITask
Set bg = tm.RunInBackground(kLater, New MyBgTask)  ' Implements ICUIBackgroundTask
bg.WaitUntilDone

cards.name: ICUIViewHost
cards.summary: A tab group of view windows (document tabs) inside the docking layout, with its views, parent dock host and screen position.
use_for: listing which documents share one tab group
merging tab groups back together
avoid: switching the active document: Document.Activate or ViewWindow.Activate is simpler
cards.how: ICUIViewWindow.ViewHost (e.g. ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.ViewHost), FrameWindow.ViewHosts, or DockItem.ViewHost.

key_members.name: DockHost
key_members.use: the dock host it sits in

key_members.name: DockItem
key_members.use: this group seen as a dock item

key_members.name: InsertView
key_members.use: move a view into this group at an index

key_members.name: InsertViewHost
key_members.use: move all views of another group into this one

gotchas: InsertViewHost moves every view of the other group; the emptied group presumably disappears (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim vh As Object, v As Object
Set vh = ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.ViewHost
For Each v In vh.Views
  Debug.Print v.Index, v.Title
Next v

cards.name: ICUIViewHosts
cards.summary: Collection of all view hosts (document tab groups) owned by one frame window.
use_for: counting tab groups before tiling or combining views
avoid: listing documents: Application.Documents is the document list
cards.how: Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.ViewHosts (ICUIFrameWindow.ViewHosts).
gotchas: Item index base is not stated in the type library; CorelDRAW collections are normally 1-based (unverified here)
cards.example:
Dim vh As Object
For Each vh In Application.FrameWork.MainFrameWindow.ViewHosts
  Debug.Print vh.ID, vh.Views.Count
Next vh

cards.name: ICUIViewWindow
cards.summary: The UI-side window (a document tab) that hosts one application view: its title, kind, tab index, screen position, activate and close calls, and a link back to the application view object.
use_for: finding a document tab's screen rectangle for a capture
floating a document into its own frame
avoid: zoom or scroll: use the document window's ActiveView
closing documents you did not open
cards.how: IVGWindow.ViewWindow (e.g. ActiveWindow.ViewWindow) or ViewHost.Views.Item(i).

key_members.name: Index
key_members.use: tab index in its view host

key_members.name: ViewHost
key_members.use: the tab group it is in

gotchas: Close on the last view of a modified document may raise a save prompt, which is modal (unverified)
AppView is a plain IDispatch; that it is the CorelDRAW Window object is unverified
cards.example:
Dim vw As Object
Set vw = ActiveWindow.ViewWindow
Debug.Print vw.Title, vw.Kind, vw.Index
Application.FrameWork.CreateFrameWindowForView vw   ' float it in its own frame

cards.name: ICUIViewWindows
cards.summary: Collection of the view windows (document tabs) inside one view host.
use_for: looping over the tabs of one tab group
avoid: every open document regardless of layout: use Application.Documents or Application.Windows
cards.how: ICUIViewHost.Views, e.g. ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.ViewHost.Views.
gotchas: Item index base is not stated in the type library; CorelDRAW collections are normally 1-based (unverified here)
cards.example:
Dim vs As Object
Set vs = ActiveWindow.ViewWindow.ViewHost.Views
Debug.Print vs.Count, vs.First.Title, vs.Last.Title
vs.First.Activate

cards.name: IImportCropHandler
cards.summary: Callback interface you implement to choose the crop rectangle of a bitmap while it is being imported; CorelDRAW calls its Crop method with the file's size and resolution.
use_for: importing photos cropped by a rule (centre square, fixed aspect) per file in a batch
avoid: a fixed crop for every file: the StructImportOptions CropLeft / CropTop / CropWidth / CropHeight properties need no handler (unverified that they apply on their own)
cropping already placed bitmaps: use a PowerClip or Bitmap.Crop
cards.how: Make a class that implements it, assign an instance to StructImportOptions.CropHandler (Application.CreateStructImportOptions) with Mode = cdrImportCrop, and pass the options to Layer.ImportEx. Crop receives IStructImportCropOptions: read FileName, ImageWidth, ImageHeight, DpiX, DpiY and set Left, Top, Width, Height.

key_members.name: Crop
key_members.use: called with IStructImportCropOptions; set the crop box and return True to go on (return meaning unverified)

gotchas: the handler only runs when the import mode is cdrImportCrop (unverified)
units of Left / Top / Width / Height are presumably image pixels (unverified)
implementing it from a VBA class is unverified
cards.example:
' class CropToSquare: Implements IImportCropHandler; its Crop sets
'   o.Left = 0: o.Top = 0: o.Width = o.ImageHeight: o.Height = o.ImageHeight
Dim opt As Object
Set opt = Application.CreateStructImportOptions
opt.Mode = cdrImportCrop
Set opt.CropHandler = New CropToSquare
ActiveLayer.ImportEx("C:\img\photo.jpg", cdrAutoSense, opt).Finish

cards.name: IImportResampleHandler
cards.summary: Callback interface you implement to set the pixel size or resolution a bitmap is resampled to while it is being imported; CorelDRAW calls its Resample method per file.
use_for: batch-importing large photos downsampled to a print resolution (e.g. 300 dpi) chosen per file
avoid: one fixed size for all files: the StructImportOptions ResampleWidth / ResampleHeight / ResampleDpiX / ResampleDpiY properties need no handler (unverified that they apply on their own)
resampling already placed bitmaps: use Bitmap.Resample
cards.how: Implement it in a class, assign it to StructImportOptions.ResampleHandler with Mode = cdrImportResample, then call Layer.ImportEx. Resample receives IStructImportResampleOptions with FileName and writable Width, Height, DpiX, DpiY.

key_members.name: Resample
key_members.use: called with IStructImportResampleOptions; set size / dpi and return True to go on (return meaning unverified)

gotchas: the handler only runs when the import mode is cdrImportResample (unverified)
implementing it from a VBA class is unverified
cards.example:
' class To300dpi: Implements IImportResampleHandler; its Resample sets o.DpiX = 300: o.DpiY = 300
Dim opt As Object
Set opt = Application.CreateStructImportOptions
opt.Mode = cdrImportResample
Set opt.ResampleHandler = New To300dpi
ActiveLayer.ImportEx("C:\img\photo.tif", cdrAutoSense, opt).Finish

cards.name: Image
cards.summary: Creatable class for a raw bitmap pixel buffer (RGB, CMYK, grayscale and other image types) that scripts can create, read and paint, then turn into a bitmap object on a layer.
use_for: generating procedural bitmaps (gradients, noise, halftone dots) inside CorelDRAW
reading pixel colours of a placed bitmap for sampling or QC
building an alpha mask to pair with a bitmap
avoid: vector artwork: use shapes
heavy image editing: Corel PHOTO-PAINT or Photoshop are the right tools
cards.how: Members live on its default interface IVGImage (Type, Width, Height, Pixel, FillArea, FlipArea, Blit, Tiles, GetCopy, ReadOnly). Get one from Document.CreateImage(ImageType, Width, Height, FillColor) or from Bitmap.Image / Bitmap.ImageAlpha; place it with Layer.CreateBitmap / CreateBitmap2 or write it back with Bitmap.SetImageData.

key_members.name: IVGImage
key_members.use: default interface that carries every member of Image

gotchas: per-pixel Pixel reads are one COM call each; use Tiles and PixelData for whole-image work
an image taken from an existing bitmap may be read-only (check ReadOnly); edit a GetCopy and write it back with Bitmap.SetImageData (unverified)
Blit's MergeMode uses cdrMergeMode (normal, multiply, screen ...), not a Photoshop blend mode name
cards.example:
Dim img As Object
Set img = ActiveDocument.CreateImage(cdrRGBColorImage, 256, 256, CreateRGBColor(255, 255, 255))
img.FillArea 0, 0, 128, 256, CreateRGBColor(230, 30, 40)
ActiveLayer.CreateBitmap2 0, 0, 2, 2, img

cards.name: ImageList
cards.summary: Creatable class for a keyed list of icons used by the UI data-binding framework (for example icons in a custom docker's list).
use_for: icons for custom add-on UI
avoid: images in the drawing: use Layer.ImportEx or the Image class
cards.how: Members live on its default interface ICUIImageList (AddImage, AddBitmap, ImageExists, RemoveImage, RemoveAll, ImageKeys, ImageCount). Usually made with Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateImageList.

key_members.name: ICUIImageList
key_members.use: default interface that carries every member of ImageList

gotchas: creating it with New from VBA (cancreate flag) is unverified; CreateImageList is the safe route
cards.example:
Dim il As Object
Set il = Application.FrameWork.Application.CreateImageList
il.AddImage "ok", "C:\icons\ok.png"

cards.name: ImageTile
cards.summary: Creatable class for one rectangular tile of an Image's pixel buffer, exposing its raw bytes for fast bulk reads and writes.
use_for: fast pixel processing of a whole bitmap (threshold, colour swap, procedural fill)
avoid: a few pixels: Image.Pixel is simpler
photo editing: use Corel PHOTO-PAINT or Photoshop
cards.how: Members live on its default interface IVGImageTile (Left, Top, Right, Bottom, Width, Height, BytesPerTile, BytesPerLine, BytesPerPixel, PixelData, ReadOnly). Get tiles from Image.Tiles.

key_members.name: IVGImageTile
key_members.use: default interface that carries every member of ImageTile

gotchas: rows can be padded: step through PixelData by BytesPerLine, not Width x BytesPerPixel
PixelData is a copied byte array; edits apply only when you assign it back (unverified)
byte order inside a pixel (RGB or BGR) is not stated; test with a known colour (unverified)
tiles of a read-only image are presumably read-only too; check the tile ReadOnly flag (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim img As Object
Set img = ActiveDocument.CreateImage(cdrRGBColorImage, 256, 256)
Dim t As Object, px() As Byte
For Each t In img.Tiles
  px = t.PixelData
  ' edit px here; one row = t.BytesPerLine bytes
  t.PixelData = px
Next t

review.changes: example used an undefined img, now created with Document.CreateImage; read-only inheritance marked unverified

cards.name: ImageTiles
cards.summary: Creatable class for the collection of pixel tiles that make up one Image buffer (the harvest's description repeats ImageTile's, but this is the collection).
use_for: looping over every tile of a bitmap for bulk pixel work
avoid: single-pixel reads: use Image.Pixel
cards.how: Members live on its default interface IVGImageTiles (Count, Item, First, Last, _NewEnum). Reached as Image.Tiles.

key_members.name: IVGImageTiles
key_members.use: default interface that carries every member of ImageTiles

gotchas: the harvested member descriptions of IVGImageTiles are copy-pasted from ImageTile (Count says 'position of the tile's top edge'); go by the types
Item index base is not stated in the type library; CorelDRAW collections are normally 1-based (unverified here)
cards.example:
Dim img As Object, tiles As Object
Set img = ActiveDocument.CreateImage(cdrRGBColorImage, 256, 256)
Set tiles = img.Tiles
Debug.Print tiles.Count, tiles.First.Width, tiles.Last.Bottom

review.changes: example used an undefined img, now created with Document.CreateImage

cards.name: ImportFilter
cards.summary: Creatable class for an import filter and its settings: the object Layer.ImportEx returns, which can show the filter's options dialog and must be finished to complete the import.
use_for: placing logos, photos, PDFs or AI files into a CorelDRAW layout from a script
batch-building catalogue pages from a folder of images
avoid: opening a file as its own document: use Application.OpenDocument
ShowDialog in unattended runs: modal
cards.how: Members live on its default interface ICorelImportFilter (Reset, Finish, HasDialog, ShowDialog), which is flagged hidden. Get it from ActiveLayer.ImportEx(FileName, Filter, Options), with options from Application.CreateStructImportOptions.

key_members.name: ICorelImportFilter
key_members.use: default interface that carries every member of ImportFilter

gotchas: the import is not complete until Finish is called on the returned object
HasDialog is a read-only Boolean saying whether the filter has an options dialog; ShowDialog(hWnd) opens it and presumably blocks the COM call (unverified)
ICorelImportFilter is flagged hidden, so its members do not show in the Object Browser by default
cards.example:
Dim opt As Object, flt As Object
Set opt = Application.CreateStructImportOptions
opt.MaintainLayers = True
Set flt = ActiveLayer.ImportEx("C:\art\logo.ai", cdrAutoSense, opt)
flt.Finish

review.changes: gotcha said HasDialog opens the options dialog (it is a read-only Boolean), fixed; AI equivalent File/Place... replaced by the scripting counterpart PlacedItems (both exist)

cards.name: INT_PTR
cards.summary: Type alias for a pointer-sized integer (int64 in the 64-bit type library). It only appears as the return type of the internal IPDFSettingsInternal._GetSettings; there is no object behind it.
use_for: reading type signatures: recognising raw-pointer values
avoid: anything a design script does: it is a typedef, not a class
cards.how: Not reached at all; it is a type name inside VGCoreAuto.tlb (also declared in CdrPDFVBA and CdrPrn).
gotchas: a value of this type is a raw native pointer; it means nothing to VBA or Python COM code
cards.example:
' no members; seen only in signatures, e.g.
' IPDFSettingsInternal._GetSettings() As INT_PTR

cards.name: IPDFSettingsInternal
cards.summary: Internal IUnknown-based interface whose only member hands back a raw pointer to the native PDF settings; it is plumbing behind the PDF export, not a scripting interface.
use_for: nothing for design scripts
avoid: PDF export settings: use Document.PDFSettings (IPDFVBASettings)
cards.how: Inherits IUnknown and is not dispatchable, so late-bound VBA / Python COM cannot call it.

key_members.name: _GetSettings
key_members.use: returns an INT_PTR raw pointer to internal settings

gotchas: not dispatchable (inherits IUnknown, no 'dispatchable' flag): late-bound calls fail
the returned value is a native pointer; dereferencing it from a script is impossible
cards.example:
' use the public interface instead:
ActiveDocument.PDFSettings.pdfVersion = pdfVersionPDFX4

cards.name: IPDFVBASettings
cards.summary: Settings for File > Publish to PDF on one document: page range, PDF version (PDF/X, PDF/A), colour mode and profile, font embedding, bitmap compression and downsampling, bleed and printer marks, spot handling, overprints and encryption, plus saving and loading PDF styles.
use_for: print-ready PDF/X-4 export of posters, packaging and brochures with bleed and crop marks
small web or email PDFs with JPEG compression and downsampling
password-protected client proofs
avoid: raster output (PNG / JPG previews): use Document.Export or ExportBitmap
ShowDialog in unattended runs: modal
cards.how: ActiveDocument.PDFSettings (IVGDocument.PDFSettings); set properties, then call ActiveDocument.PublishToPDF(path).

key_members.name: Reset
key_members.use: back to defaults before building a setting set

key_members.name: Load
key_members.use: load a saved PDF style by name

key_members.name: Save
key_members.use: save the current settings as a style

key_members.name: ShowDialog
key_members.use: open the Publish to PDF dialog (modal)

key_members.name: PageRange
key_members.use: page list such as "1-3,5", used with pdfPageRange

key_members.name: pdfVersion
key_members.use: compatibility: pdfVersion12 ... pdfVersion17_Acrobat9, PDF/X-1, X-1a, X-3, X-4, PDF/A-1b

key_members.name: OutputSpotColorsAs
key_members.use: keep spots or convert to RGB / CMYK / gray

gotchas: PageRange is used only when PublishRange = pdfPageRange
Bleed's description says 'tens of micron'; CorelDRAW's internal unit is 0.1 micron, so check the unit on a test export (unverified)
EmbedFilename (string) and EmbedFile (bool) have their descriptions swapped in the type library; go by the types
SpotColors and ConvertSpotColors are hidden members; use OutputSpotColorsAs
settings stay on the document between exports (unverified); call Reset first for a predictable result
ShowDialog blocks the COM call until a person closes it

PublishRange = 1 (pdfCurrentPage) publishes the current page only; the default exports every page, including a hidden masters page a scene may carry, so a one-page design came out as a 2-page PDF (plan runs 2026-10-15 (print_prep.pdfx_export)).
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PDFSettings
  .Reset
  .PublishRange = pdfPageRange
  .PageRange = "1-2"
  .pdfVersion = pdfVersionPDFX4
  .IncludeBleed = True
End With
ActiveDocument.PublishToPDF "C:\out\poster.pdf"

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintDocument
cards.summary: Opaque, hidden handle for one document inside a multi-document print job; the type library declares no members on it.
use_for: passing a document to PrintJob.AddDocument (the parameter type)
avoid: reading anything from it: it has no members; use the CorelDRAW Document instead
cards.how: Appears as the parameter type of PrintJob.AddDocument and as PrintJob.Documents.Item; flagged hidden.

key_members.name: IDispatch
key_members.use: only inherited dispatch plumbing; no members of its own

gotchas: no members: treat it as an opaque token
that PrintJob.AddDocument accepts a normal CorelDRAW Document for this parameter is unverified
cards.example: Application.PrintJob.AddDocument ActiveDocument, "1"   ' passes the document as IPrnVBAPrintDocument

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintDocuments
cards.summary: Hidden collection of the documents queued in the application's multi-document print job.
use_for: checking how many documents a print job holds before PrintOut
avoid: adding documents: use PrintJob.AddDocument
cards.how: Application.PrintJob.Documents (IPrnVBAPrintJob.Documents).

key_members.name: Count
key_members.use: number of documents in the job

gotchas: Item is itself a hidden member and returns the member-less IPrnVBAPrintDocument, so there is little to read from it
Item index base is not stated in the type library; CorelDRAW collections are normally 1-based (unverified here)
cards.example:
With Application.PrintJob
  .Clear
  .AddDocument ActiveDocument
  Debug.Print .Documents.Count
End With

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrinter
cards.summary: One installed printer as CorelDRAW sees it: name, driver, port, default / ready state, PostScript and colour capability, its properties dialog and the page-size matching switch.
use_for: picking a colour PostScript device for proofs
checking a printer is ready before a batch print
avoid: PDF output: use Document.PublishToPDF
ShowDialog in unattended runs: modal
cards.how: ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Printer (writable), Application.Printers.Item(i) or Application.Printers.Default. Flagged hidden.

key_members.name: Name
key_members.use: printer name, as used by PrintSettings.SelectPrinter

key_members.name: Default
key_members.use: True for the Windows default printer

key_members.name: Ready
key_members.use: True when the printer reports ready

key_members.name: ColorEnabled
key_members.use: True when colour output is enabled

key_members.name: ShowDialog
key_members.use: open the driver's Printer Properties dialog (modal)

gotchas: Type is the driver name, not an enum
ShowDialog opens the driver dialog and blocks the COM call
Ready only reflects what the driver reports; a network printer can say ready and still fail (unverified)
cards.example:
Dim p As Object
Set p = Application.Printers.Default
If p.Ready And p.ColorEnabled Then ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.SelectPrinter p.Name

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrinters
cards.summary: Hidden collection of the printers installed in Windows, with the system default printer.
use_for: listing printers to choose a proofing device
finding the default printer
avoid: changing the Windows default printer: not possible here
cards.how: Application.Printers (IVGApplication.Printers).
gotchas: Item index base is not stated in the type library; CorelDRAW collections are normally 1-based (unverified here)
it has no Find or name lookup; loop and compare Name
cards.example:
Dim i As Long
For i = 1 To Application.Printers.Count
  Debug.Print Application.Printers.Item(i).Name
Next i
Debug.Print Application.Printers.Default.Name

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintJob
cards.summary: The application-wide multi-document print job: queue documents (or page ranges of them), reach the job's print settings, and send everything to the printer in one go.
use_for: printing several documents or page ranges as one job
batch proof printing
avoid: a single document: ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.PrintOut is simpler
PDF output: use Document.PublishToPDF
cards.how: Application.PrintJob (IVGApplication.PrintJob). Clear it, AddDocument each document with an optional page range, adjust Settings (IPrnVBAPrintSettings), then PrintOut. Flagged hidden.

key_members.name: AddDocument
key_members.use: queue a document, optionally only a page range

key_members.name: PrintOut
key_members.use: send the job to the printer

gotchas: PrintOut sends the job to the printer (presumably without a dialog, unverified), on real paper; for tests set Settings.PrintToFile = True and Settings.FileName
the job is application-wide (Application.PrintJob) and may still hold earlier additions (unverified); call Clear first
AddDocument is typed for IPrnVBAPrintDocument; passing a CorelDRAW Document is unverified
AddPage is a hidden member
cards.example:
With Application.PrintJob
  .Clear
  .AddDocument ActiveDocument, "1-2"
  .Settings.PrintToFile = True
  .Settings.FileName = "C:\out\job.prn"
  .PrintOut
End With

review.changes: PrintOut 'no dialog' and the job keeping earlier additions were stated as fact; marked unverified

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintLayout
cards.summary: Hidden print-layout settings of a document: how the page is placed on the printer sheet (as in document, fit, centred, corners, custom), bleed limit, and tiling of oversized pages with tiling marks and overlap.
use_for: fitting an A3 poster onto an A4 proof sheet
tiling a large banner across several sheets
limiting bleed on printed proofs
avoid: imposition of several pages per sheet: not covered by this interface
PDF bleed: use PDFSettings.IncludeBleed / Bleed
cards.how: ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Layout (IPrnVBAPrintSettings.Layout).

key_members.name: BleedLimit
key_members.use: bleed amount kept around the page

key_members.name: PrintTiledPages
key_members.use: split a large page across printer sheets

gotchas: BleedLimit and TileOverlap are doubles in an unstated unit, presumably document units (unverified)
bleed only prints if the artwork already extends past the page edge
prnPlaceCustom needs offsets this interface does not expose (unverified)
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Layout
  .Placement = prnPlaceFitToPage
  .UseBleedLimit = True
  .BleedLimit = 0.125
End With

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintOptions
cards.summary: Hidden miscellaneous print options of a document: which object types print (vectors, bitmaps, text), colour mode and colour profile, text in black, fountain steps, whole-page rasterizing, bitmap downsampling, and the job information sheet contents.
use_for: fast grayscale or text-only proofs
rasterizing complex transparency for a problem printer
suppressing the job information sheet in batch prints
avoid: PDF export settings: use Document.PDFSettings
leaving PrintVectors / PrintBitmaps / PrintText off after a proof: later prints silently drop those objects
cards.how: ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Options (IPrnVBAPrintSettings.Options).

key_members.name: ObjectsColorMode
key_members.use: colour mode all objects are output in

key_members.name: UseColorProfile
key_members.use: apply the ICC profile while printing

key_members.name: PreservePureBlack
key_members.use: keep pure black in colour conversions

key_members.name: MarksToPage
key_members.use: keep printer marks inside the page area

gotchas: PrintVectors / PrintBitmaps / PrintText = False drop those objects without warning; set them back
RasterizeResolution matters only when RasterizePage = True
BitmapColorMode is a hidden member; ObjectsColorMode is the visible switch (relationship unverified)
settings live on the document's PrintSettings; PrintSettings.Reset gives a clean start
cards.example:
With ActiveDocument.PrintSettings.Options
  .ColorMode = prnModeGrayscale
  .PrintBitmaps = False
  .JobInformation = False
End With

cards.name: IPrnVBAPrintPage
cards.summary: Opaque, hidden handle for one page queued in a print job; the type library declares no members on it.
use_for: counting or passing pages of a print job (PrintJob.Pages, PrintJob.AddPage)
avoid: reading page content or size: use the CorelDRAW Page object
cards.how: Returned by PrintJob.Pages.Item(i) and taken by the hidden PrintJob.AddPage; flagged hidden.

key_members.name: IDispatch
key_members.use: only inherited dispatch plumbing; no members of its own

gotchas: no members: treat it as an opaque token
AddPage, the call that takes it, is itself a hidden member
cards.example: Debug.Print Application.PrintJob.Pages.Count   ' Pages.Item(i) returns IPrnVBAPrintPage
